content.text:
This looks very feasible—roughly a small, focused UI change once the remaining manifests arrive.

The current spell sheet is a 10×10 atlas of 32px icons with 95 entries, mapped by ID in [manifest.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/assets/icons/spells/manifest.js). The clean path is:

- Add `iconId`/atlas metadata to the existing spell-bar action objects in [hudFeeds.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main/ui/hudFeeds.js).
- Render the atlas icon in both desktop HUD and mobile [spellDock.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/display/ui/spellDock.js).
- Keep spell names, costs, cooldowns, tooltips, accessibility labels, and Unicode fallback intact.
- Later reuse the same resolver for VIS/status badges and inventory/tooltips.

The VIS layer is also a good candidate. It currently resolves through the `VIS` table and Unicode glyphs in [hud.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/display/ui/hud.js), with status metadata assembled in [statusDisplayMetadata.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main/ui/statusDisplayMetadata.js). I’d make icons an optional visual field, not replace the semantic status data.

On compression:

- Current PNG: 2.6 MB.
- JPEG quality 2: ~1.0 MB.
- JPEG quality 6: ~514 KB.
- WebP quality 75: ~322 KB.

JPEG is not lossless and is a poor fit for this pixel art: it can introduce ringing and muddy dark edges around 32px icons. I’d prefer:

1. Keep the source PNG for authoring.
2. Generate an optimized indexed PNG or lossless WebP for shipping.
3. Use the PNG as a fallback only if needed.

2.6 MB is technically acceptable for one desktop asset, but targeting roughly 300–600 KB would be worthwhile, especially for mobile. I haven’t changed the repository; I only inspected the assets and tested temporary compression copies. The existing game display remains unaffected—the new art can be confined to menus, bars, inventory, tooltips, and VIS.

wow -- that is absolutely amazing -- I have no idea how to "maintain" this -- but I absolutely love the outcome.

That makes me genuinely happy—this is exactly the kind of visual identity layer the game was ready for.

Maintenance is intentionally simple:

- Add an atlas entry with the canonical ID and coordinates.
- Keep the sheet WebP aligned to the manifest grid.
- The renderer automatically discovers the grid size.
- If anything is missing or mistyped, Unicode fallback keeps the UI safe.

So adding future spell, item, or status art should mostly be “add the sprite, add one manifest entry.”
